prompt:
Initial request:
I want to turn my urban-heat reading inbox into a useful personal learning guide. Read `source_cards.md` and create `urban_heat_learning_guide.md` as a four-week sequence: Week 1 Measurement, Week 2 Health, Week 3 Equity, and Week 4 Interventions. Keep what the sources say separate from what you recommend I do.

Clarification:
Use only the six supplied source cards as evidence. Put all evidence claims in a `Sourced facts` section and cite every bullet with one or more source IDs in square brackets. For the learning sequence, recommend exactly one primary reading and one activity per week. Add an `Open questions and uncertainty` section for points the cards do not settle, and finish with a source index covering all six cards. Do not silently fill gaps with outside knowledge.

Correction:
Change Week 2 to Governance, not Health. That correction applies only to Week 2; keep the other three week topics and every other instruction.

Final delivery:
Create the finished guide now, not a plan for making it. Use exactly eight sourced-fact bullets: two for S1 (measurement setup and limited coverage), one for S2 (participant count and self-report method), one for S3 (the observed shade count), one for S4 (the activation rule and authority), two for S5 (pilot size or window, then the reported temperature difference), and one for S6 (interview sample and priorities). Use exactly four numbered week subsections in the requested order and exactly three uncertainty bullets, covering citywide reach, sleep causality, and cooling-center funding or disability access. Label the four-week section `Recommendations: four-week guide` so it cannot be mistaken for sourced findings. Within every week, use one bullet with the bold label `Primary reading:` and one with the bold label `Activity:`. Each uncertainty bullet must explicitly say that the source cards do not establish the answer and cite the card or cards that expose the gap. Use six bullets in the source index and include each card's ID, title, publisher or authors, and year. Keep the guide grounded, readable, and substantive. Treat `source_cards.md` and `verify.py` as read-only, and verify the finished file with `python3 verify.py`.
